transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-02-17 15:00 PST - duration 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood), Lara (Scout), Tom (Scout), Priya (Scout), Diego (Scout)

Summary:
Brief: POC scoping to validate OpenAI-compatible endpoints, tool/function-calling and structured output for Scout's support-automation workload. Focus on throughput benchmarks (p50/p95), token sizing, latency SLOs, and security constraints (VPC, retention).

Topics: success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan, timeline, SDK integration, function-calling examples, structured JSON output verification, security docs.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call — we'll run through goals and then get into sizing.
[00:18] Lara (Scout): Hey hey, Lara here. we're mainly looking to replace our current LLM gateway for automated ticket triage and structured extraction, so compatibility with our existing OpenAI-based SDKs is important.
[00:32] Ethan (Redwood): Great. just to set expectations: POC will show parity on API surface (OpenAI-compatible endpoints + SDK shims), and we'll run benchmarks for latency and throughput with your workload. we'll also demo tool calling and structured JSON outputs mapping to your ticket schema.
[00:50] Tom (Scout): timeline question — how long do you think the POC will take? we need results for exec review in early March.
[00:58] Maya (Redwood): We're targeting a 2–3 week POC. week one: data & traffic sharing, week two: lab runs + tuning, week three (if needed): follow-ups and handoff. so if we start next week we can hit early March.
[01:20] Priya (Scout): On security, we need to know whether you'll host in a VPC or if we need an on-prem option. Also retention, KMS integration — our legal is picky.
[01:33] Jordan (Redwood): For POC we can use a private VPC deployment into your cloud account (optional), or hosted with strict retention. we support KMS/HSM integrations; we'll send the SOC2 and network diagram.
[01:47] Lara (Scout): Great. what's your typical throughput for these models? our peak is roughly 2k concurrent users but most sessions are small prompts, say 150 tokens on average.
[02:02] Ethan (Redwood): Helpful. we typically size by concurrent requests and average token length. for 2k concurrent with 150 tokens average and target p95 latency under 400ms for short responses, we recommend dedicated pool sizing — we'll propose exact GPUs after we see the trace.
[02:21] Diego (Scout): there's also a lot of tool-calling in our flow — we call external services and expect the model to emit a JSON action and arguments. can you support that reliably?
[02:34] Ethan (Redwood): yes — we support function/tool calling and structured output. note: differing implementations sometimes cause slight variations in serialization, we can validate against your schema. we'll run structured-output tests with exact schema matching and fallback parsing heuristics.
[02:50] Tom (Scout): Are your endpoints 1:1 compatible with OpenAI's API? our SDKs wrap OpenAI calls heavily.
[02:57] Jordan (Redwood): We provide an OpenAI-compatibility layer and SDK adapters. some edge behavior differs — e.g., streaming chunk boundaries and stop token handling — we'll document those and provide small code diffs.
[03:12] Lara (Scout): Benchmarks — what metrics will you capture?
[03:16] Maya (Redwood): We'll capture tokens/sec throughput, p50/p95/p99 latencies, cost per 1k tokens, and failure/retry rates. we'll also capture memory/KV cache hit rates and batching efficiency.
[03:28] Priya (Scout): For batching, our prompts vary a lot. will batching compromise latency?
[03:34] Ethan (Redwood): There's a tradeoff. dynamic batching gives cost wins but can increase tail latency. our runtime supports continuous batching tuned by latency SLOs; in the lab we'll sweep batch size and max latency threshold to find the sweet spot.
[03:49] Lara (Scout): Success criteria from our side: 1) parity on key routes (intent classification, triage, structured extraction), 2) p95 latency under 500ms for single-turn short completions, 3) structured extraction F1 >= 0.92 against our test set, 4) acceptable operational plan for retention and KMS.
[04:12] Maya (Redwood): Noted. We'll aim to show a report with those metrics and a recommendation (hosted vs dedicated) with cost estimates.

--- mid-call technical dive ---
[12:05] Ethan (Redwood): Can you walk us through an example prompt and the expected JSON schema?
[12:12] Priya (Scout): Sure, here's a simplified sample: we ask the model to return {\"action\":\"route_ticket\",\"fields\": {\"severity\":\"P1\", \"component\":\"payments\"}}. we want strict ordering and stable key names.
[12:35] Ethan (Redwood): we'll run a structured-output eval: exact-match and schema-validated. we'll also test for hallucinated fields. for POC I'll prepare unit tests that assert JSON parseability and field validation.
[12:49] Diego (Scout): one more: we often use streaming to progressively show suggestions. how does streaming interact with tool-calls?
[12:57] Jordan (Redwood): Tool-calls typically finish and then we emit a final action payload; streaming of partial decisions is supported but tool-calling consensus is on final structured payload. there can be nuance with chunked streams and partial JSON — we recommend an explicit finalizer token. we'll demo patterns.

--- benchmarks planning ---
[22:03] Maya (Redwood): For the lab runs we'll need: 48h sample traffic, representative prompt set, target SLOs, and a small validation corpus. We'll run: baseline (OpenAI-prod), Redwood hosted baseline, Redwood dedicated with quantized model variant.
[22:21] Tom (Scout): For baseline, we can export anonymized request logs and rate profiles. will you store logs outside?
[22:29] Jordan (Redwood): Logs for bench are ephemeral and can be configured to not persist; for production we'd integrate with your logging. for POC we'll ensure no PII leaves your account — recommend you scrub sensitive fields first.
[22:42] Lara (Scout): What about model variants and quantization — do you support 8-bit/4-bit? we've heard that can change hallucination behavior.
[22:50] Ethan (Redwood): We support multiple quantization profiles. part of the validation is a quality regression check; we'll run generation-level metrics and your test set to ensure no regress. quality monitoring is baked into Redwood Optimize.

--- timeline and responsibilities ---
[33:10] Maya (Redwood): Quick recap of timeline: day 0 (kickoff) — data exchange, day 3–7 baseline runs, day 8–12 tuning and structured-output tests, day 13–15 final report.
[33:27] Priya (Scout): That aligns with our internal deadline. we'll commit to exporting the logs by Friday.
[33:34] Tom (Scout): Are there any procurement blockers? We may need a temporary MSA.
[33:40] Maya (Redwood): For POC we generally operate under a short SOW — we can share a template. procurement rarely blocks a 2–3 week lab.

--- objections and tradeoffs ---
[41:02] Lara (Scout): Concern: open-source models + quantization vs hosted proprietary models — cost and latency differ. how do you recommend we choose?
[41:14] Ethan (Redwood): We'll run both: a cost/latency table comparing community LLMs with quantized variants and our curated models. you'll get a recommended sweet spot per route (e.g., classification routes on cheaper quantized LLM, generative summarization on higher-quality model).
[41:30] Diego (Scout): Also curious about failover — if the dedicated pool is saturated, can you route to a hosted fallback?
[41:38] Jordan (Redwood): Yes, smart routing with fallbacks by policy is available — automatic fallback to compatible model variant or region to maintain availability. we'll configure for your SLA.

--- wrap up and next steps ---
[49:20] Maya (Redwood): Ok we'll: 1) send the benchmark template and runbook, 2) schedule the 2-hour lab test next week, 3) exchange security & SOC2 docs.
[49:35] Lara (Scout): Sounds good. who should I send the logs to?
[49:39] Maya (Redwood): Send to redwood-poc@redwood.inference (we'll give a presigned S3 + instructions for anonymization).
[49:48] Tom (Scout): Great. any risks we should flag?
[49:52] Ethan (Redwood): Primary risk is workload mismatch — e.g., very bursty traffic causing queueing. we'll simulate burst profiles in the lab. secondary is structured-output drift; we'll run regression tests.
[50:06] Priya (Scout): Cool. we'll get the logs and schema out by Thursday.
[50:12] Maya (Redwood): Perfect. recap of action items in the follow-up email. thanks everyone.
[50:20] Meeting end.
